repository.name: @webex/common-timers
repository.purpose: Timer primitives for the Cisco Webex JS SDK that never hold a Node process open: unref-ing wrappers over setTimeout and setInterval, plus a restartable one-shot Timer with a guarded init-running-done lifecycle.

modules.coverage_evidence: Field coverage 100% (14/14) assessed 2026-09-24; critical field coverage 9/9. Test coverage is incomplete: the unit suite is 13 tests in 1 file (test/unit/spec/index.ts), all passing as of 2026-10-05. That suite is pre-existing and was not authored by this specification change. MOD-002, MOD-004, MOD-009 and MOD-012 have no automated evidence and are scored Weak; MOD-001 and MOD-003 are partly covered. Nothing asserts that unref() is called, so the package's core guarantee rests on code reading rather than on a test. This module has no characterization baseline, so the Timer constructor's missing duration validation is specified but unpinned; it was triaged on 2026-09-24 as fix-separately and the caller-facing hazard is recorded in the module spec under Pitfalls and constraints. Independent validation by codex ran four times across 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-28, but that assessment covered a test suite that has since been withdrawn from this change, so it is stale and revalidation is required. Promotion to Specced is held pending unref and re-entrancy assertions, a characterization baseline, and a clean validator run.

common-timers-sdk.summary: Published npm package export surface declared by main and devMain: safeSetTimeout and safeSetInterval, which return the platform timer handle after unref-ing it where that is supported, and the Timer class, a restartable one-shot timer whose start, reset, and cancel methods throw on an invalid lifecycle transition. Per-export detail lives in the owning module spec Public surface.

host-timer-api.source: Host JavaScript runtime timer API: setTimeout, setInterval, and clearTimeout, plus the Node.js Timeout.unref() extension
host-timer-api.summary: The platform scheduling primitives the module wraps. Node returns a Timeout object carrying unref(); browsers return a numeric handle without it, which is why every wrapper feature-detects unref rather than assuming a platform.
